newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Robotics to offer free x2 standard upgrade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Robotics to offer free x2 standard upgrade.

text.p: U.S. Robotics Corp said Wednesday it launched a customer satisfaction program for its X2 high-speed modems and systems hubs, including free upgrades to the international standard expected next year.
In a conference call with reporters, the Skokie, Illinois-based company said it does not expect to take any special charges related to the program.

U.S. Robotics said the program also gives buyers of new x2 desktop and PC card modems one month of free Internet service worth up to $25 with a provider using x2, plus a 30-day "satisfaction guaranteed" return policy. U.S. Robotics said some 350 Internet Service Providers currently offer x2 connections.
U.S. Robotics, whose merger with 3Com Corp is expected to close next month, began offering in February its x2 technology. It allows connections to the Internet at speeds up to 56 kilobits per second.
An alliance of other companies, led by Rockwell International Corp and Motorola Inc, also offers 56K technology. But, as there is currently no standard, their technology and x2 do not work together.
U.S. Robotics chairman and chief executive Casey Cowell said the company does not disclose specific sales figures but said the x2 technology has been "very broadly accepted".

"Every new generation of speed has been more rapidly accepted in the marketplace than the prior generations, and that's true of x2 right now," Cowell said. "We are just putting the pedal right to the floor."

Under the U.S. Robotics' program, called "x2 Delivers", the company said it will give upgrades to the International Telecommunication Union (ITU-T) 56K modem standard which it expects to be adopted in 1998.
U.S. Robotics said the free upgrades will be available for all its x2 products used by consumers, internet service providers and corporations.
U.S. Robotics modems run on chips produced by Texas Instruments Inc which can be enhanced with software.
The company said the standard upgrades will be simple, using software downloaded from U.S. Robotics' web site, or it will replace the modems with ones that meet the standard.
"We're very familiar with the technology and what's involved for doing a software upgrade," Cowell said.
"We don't anticipate there will be any sort of a special charge or unusual expense at all," he said, declining to disclose the expected overall cost of the program.
The free Internet service offer is available to buyers of retail modems between June 1 and September 15.
